questions.question: At a simple interest rate of 8% per annum, how much amount (in ₹ units) will be the simple interest amount of ₹700 in 2 years?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Calculate the **Effective Interest Rate**: 8% × 2 years = 16%.

Since 16% of the **Principal** equals the **Simple Interest** (₹700):

Principal = (700 ÷ 16) × 100

Principal = 43.75 × 100 = 4375.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4375.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given values from the problem:

⇒ **Simple Interest (SI)** = ₹700

⇒ **Rate of Interest (R)** = 8% per annum

⇒ **Time Period (T)** = 2 years

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/21b9cd3d7e5bb0d7a3e418e01b3f86bd917293e5fee8feae2208e3802faebcb1.png] 

Formula used for **Simple Interest**:

⇒ SI = (P × R × T) / 100

Substitute the given values to find the **Principal (P)**:

⇒ 700 = (P × 8 × 2) / 100

⇒ 700 = (P × 16) / 100

⇒ P × 16 = 700 × 100

⇒ P = 70000 / 16

⇒ P = 4375

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4375.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount in Simple Interest

The total amount (A) after T years is the sum of the Principal and the interest: A = P + SI = P(1 + RT/100).

Compound Interest (CI)

Interest is calculated on the principal and the accumulated interest: A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ.

SI vs CI Difference

For a period of 2 years, the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest is given by: D = P(r/100)².

questions.question: If 2 tan A = 3 , what is the value of (sec A + tan A - 1)(sec A - tan A + 1) ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rewrite the expression **(sec A + tan A − 1)(sec A − tan A + 1)** as **[sec A + (tan A − 1)][sec A − (tan A − 1)]**.

Applying the **difference of squares** identity **(x + y)(x − y) = x² − y²**:

Expression = **sec² A − (tan A − 1)²** = **sec² A − (tan² A − 2 tan A + 1)**.

Using **sec² A − tan² A = 1**, it simplifies to: **(sec² A − tan² A) + 2 tan A − 1 = 1 + 2 tan A − 1 = 2 tan A**.

Since it is given that **2 tan A = 3**, the final value is **3**.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 2 tan A = 3 ⇒ **tan A = 3/2**

**Formula Used:** In a right-angled triangle, **tan A = Perpendicular / Base** and **sec A = Hypotenuse / Base**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/84c0f34b390878837cff12707b687644f74e3606da5f260efd8e4c6f1d3ee0de.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **Perpendicular (P) = 3** and **Base (B) = 2**.

⇒ **Hypotenuse (H)** = √(3² + 2²) = √(9 + 4) = **√13**.

⇒ **sec A** = H / B = **√13 / 2** and **tan A** = 3 / 2.

⇒ Expression = (√13/2 + 3/2 − 1) × (√13/2 − 3/2 + 1)

⇒ [(√13 + 3 − 2) / 2] × [(√13 − 3 + 2) / 2]

⇒ [(√13 + 1) / 2] × [(√13 − 1) / 2]

⇒ (√13 + 1)(√13 − 1) / 4

⇒ (13 − 1) / 4 = 12 / 4 = **3**.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Pythagorean Identities

Fundamental relations: **sin² A + cos² A = 1**, **1 + tan² A = sec² A**, and **1 + cot² A = cosec² A**.

Difference of Squares

The algebraic identity **(a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²** is frequently used to simplify trigonometric products involving conjugate pairs.

Reciprocal Relations

Definitions based on a right triangle: **sec A = 1/cos A**, **cosec A = 1/sin A**, and **tan A = sin A / cos A**.

questions.question: Given that 74⁰.⁴⁵ = x , 74⁰.¹² = y and x^z = y² , then the value of z is close to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Directly equate the **powers** since the base **74** is common to both **x** and **y**.

From **xz = y²**, the relationship is: **(Power of x) × z = (Power of y) × 2**.

Substitute the given exponents: **0.45 × z = 0.12 × 2**.

**0.45z = 0.24** ⇒ **z = 24 ÷ 45 = 8/15 ≈ 0.53**.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.53.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**x = 74⁰.⁴⁵**

**y = 74⁰.¹²**

**xz = y²**

**Method Used:** Apply **Laws of Indices** for powers of the same base.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Substitute **x** and **y** in the equation **xz = y²**:

⇒ (74⁰.⁴⁵)z = (74⁰.¹²)²

⇒ 74⁽⁰.⁴⁵ × z⁾ = 74⁽⁰.¹² × ²⁾

⇒ 74⁰.⁴⁵z = 74⁰.²⁴

⇒ Since the **bases** are equal, their **exponents** must also be equal:

⇒ 0.45z = 0.24

⇒ z = 0.24 ÷ 0.45

⇒ z = 24/45

⇒ z = 8/15 ≈ 0.533

**∴ The correct answer is 0.53.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Power Rule of Indices

For any non-zero base **a**, the rule **(am)ⁿ = am × ⁿ** states that raising a power to another power involves multiplying the exponents.

Equality of Exponential Expressions

If **ax = ay** and **a** is a positive constant (**a ≠ 1**), then the exponents **x** and **y** must be equal (**x = y**).

Product Rule of Indices

When multiplying two expressions with the same base, add the exponents: **am × aⁿ = am ⁺ ⁿ**.

questions.question: In a family, the sum of the ages of a father and son is 50 years. 10 years from now, the difference in their ages will be 20 years. Find the ratio of the son's age to the father's age.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The age **difference** between two people always remains **constant** over time.

Difference = 20 years | Sum = 50 years.

Father's age = (Sum + Difference) ÷ 2 = (50 + 20) ÷ 2 = 35 years.

Son's age = (Sum − Difference) ÷ 2 = (50 − 20) ÷ 2 = 15 years.

Ratio of **Son** to **Father** = 15 : 35 = 3 : 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 3:7.**

questions.question: A trapezium has parallel sides of lengths 17 cm and 29 cm, and the distance between them is 15 cm. What is the area of the trapezium?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Area** of a **trapezium** is simply the **product** of the **average** of the **parallel sides** and the **height**.

Average of parallel sides = (17 + 29) ÷ 2 = 23 cm

Area = Average × Height = 23 × 15 = 345 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 345 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of first **parallel side** (a) = 17 cm

Length of second **parallel side** (b) = 29 cm

**Height** (distance between them, h) = 15 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of Trapezium = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × Height

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/71890ec11765d18ed086ed0a4fe5cabe26b336ec04e5c5f4baf8a3d6333c882a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = 1/2 × (17 + 29) × 15

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 46 × 15

⇒ Area = 23 × 15

⇒ Area = 345 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 345 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perimeter of a Trapezium

The total boundary length of a trapezium is the sum of all its four sides: **Perimeter = a + b + c + d**.

Median of a Trapezium

The **median** is the line segment connecting the midpoints of the non-parallel sides. Its length is the average of the parallel sides: **Median = (a + b) ÷ 2**.

Isosceles Trapezium

A trapezium where the **non-parallel sides** are equal in length and the **base angles** are equal.

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by both 17 and 13?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since **17** and **13** are both **prime numbers**, any number divisible by both must be divisible by their **LCM**.

**LCM(17, 13)** = 17 × 13 = **221**.

Check for a multiple of **221**: 221 × 100 = 22100. The nearest value is 21658.

22100 − 21658 = 442. Since 442 ÷ 221 = 2, then 21658 is exactly divisible.

questions.question: In a class, there are 36 boys and 24 girls. By what percentage should the number of girls be increased so that it becomes equal to the number of boys?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Boys** to **Girls** = 36 : 24 = 3 : 2.

To make the number of **Girls** (2 units) equal to **Boys** (3 units), the increase needed = 3 − 2 = 1 unit.

Percentage increase = (Increase / Initial units of girls) × 100.

Percentage increase = (1 / 2) × 100 = 50%.

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of **Boys** = 36

Number of **Girls** = 24

**Formula Used:**

Percentage Increase = [(Target Value − Original Value) / Original Value] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8c0b213937a8d87c1e310304d4e3921a40eb546b05be2e078037a4c7a76a7c1f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Target number of **Girls** = 36

⇒ Required increase in **Girls** = 36 − 24 = 12

⇒ Percentage increase = (12 / 24) × 100

⇒ Percentage increase = (1 / 2) × 100

⇒ Percentage increase = 50%

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Increase vs Decrease

Percentage change is always calculated on the **original (base) value**. Increase % = (Difference / Original) × 100.

Fractional Conversion

1/2 = 50%, 1/3 = 33.33%, 1/4 = 25%, 1/5 = 20%. Knowing these helps in solving **Quantitative Aptitude** questions faster.

Base Change Property

If A is 50% more than B, then B is 33.33% less than A. The percentage value changes when the **base value** is shifted.

questions.question: If 40 pages are printed in 5 minutes by a printer, how many pages will be printed in 3 hours?

Rate of **printer** = 40 ÷ 5 = 8 pages/min.

Total time in minutes = 3 × 60 = 180 min.

Total **pages** printed = 180 × 8 = 1440.

**∴ The correct answer is 1440 pages.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Time taken = 5 min

⇒ Conversion of **time**: 1 hr = 60 min

⇒ 3 hr = 3 × 60 = 180 min

⇒ Pages printed in 1 min = 40 ÷ 5 = 8 pages

⇒ Pages printed in 180 min = 180 × 8

⇒ Total **pages** = 1440

**∴ The correct answer is 1440 pages.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

questions.question: If a + b =12 and ab=8 then the numerical value of ((a)/(b)+(b)/(a)) will be:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The expression (a/b + b/a) simplifies to (a² + b²) / ab.

Using the identity (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab, we get a² + b² = (a + b)² − 2ab.

Substitute values: [12² − 2 × 8] / 8.

Value = [144 − 16] / 8 = 128 / 8 = 16.

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

a + b = 12

ab = 8

**Formula Used:**

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a61509d4d72dc44899b14d5ec987bcdae8efd2045dcdee7153adb61ea939a732.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Target expression = a/b + b/a

⇒ By taking **LCM** of denominators: (a² + b²) / ab

⇒ We know (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

⇒ 12² = a² + b² + 2(8)

⇒ 144 = a² + b² + 16

⇒ a² + b² = 144 − 16 = 128

⇒ Putting this in target: 128 / 8 = 16

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity for Squares

(a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab. This can be used to find a² + b² if the difference and product are known.

Sum of Cubes

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) or a³ + b³ = (a + b)³ − 3ab(a + b).

Relationship between Identities

(a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab. This relates the sum, difference, and product of two numbers.

questions.question: Find the third proportional to a³ − b³ and a² + b² + ab, when a = 16 and b = 12.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Third Proportional** (x) to A and B is given by **x = B² ÷ A**.

Given: A = a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²) and B = a² + b² + ab.

x = (a² + ab + b²)² ÷ [(a − b)(a² + ab + b²)] = (a² + ab + b²) ÷ (a − b).

Substitute a = 16 and b = 12: x = (16² + 12² + 16 × 12) ÷ (16 − 12) = 592 ÷ 4 = 148.

**∴ The correct answer is 148.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **a = 16** and **b = 12**. We need to find the **third proportional** to A = (a³ − b³) and B = (a² + b² + ab).

**Formula:** If x is the third proportional to A and B, then **A : B :: B : x**, which means **x = B²/A**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/62bccb8d59a13e545f2407774ec16d089b8afc8a0f609d4ddd0be451388914df.png] 

⇒ A = a³ − b³ = (16 − 12)(16² + 16 × 12 + 12²)

⇒ A = 4 × (256 + 192 + 144) = 4 × 592 = 2368

⇒ B = a² + b² + ab = 16² + 12² + 16 × 12 = 256 + 144 + 192 = 592

⇒ Third Proportional x = B² ÷ A = (592 × 592) ÷ 2368

⇒ x = (592 × 592) ÷ (4 × 592)

⇒ x = 592 ÷ 4 = 148

**∴ The correct answer is 148.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is √(ab).

Fourth Proportional

If a, b, c, d are in proportion (a:b = c:d), then the fourth proportional d = (b × c) ÷ a.

questions.question: When one-third of a number is increased by 10, the result is 65. Find the sum of the digits of the original number.
questions.solution:
Logic followed here is to translate the given mathematical statement into a linear equation to find the unknown number and then calculate the sum of its digits.

**Step 1: Let the original number be x.**

According to the given condition:

**One-third of the number** increased by **10** results in **65**.

This can be written mathematically as:

(1 / 3) × x + 10 = 65

 

**Step 2: Solve the equation for x:**

(1 / 3) × x = 65 − 10

(1 / 3) × x = 55

To isolate x, multiply both sides by 3:

x = 55 × 3

**x = 165**

The **original number** is **165**.

 

**Step 3: Find the sum of the digits:**

The digits of the number 165 are **1, 6, and 5**.

Sum of digits = 1 + 6 + 5

**Sum of digits = 12**

 

Therefore, the sum of the digits of the original number is **12**.

questions.question: The salary of Mina is ₹ 80,000. Out of which she deposits x% amount at 15% simple interest. If the accumulated amount for the money deposited after 3 years is ₹ 17,400, then find the value of x.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective **Interest Rate** for 3 years = 15% × 3 = 45%.

**Accumulated Amount** = 100% (Principal) + 45% (Interest) = 145%.

145% of **Principal** = ₹ 17,400 ⇒ **Principal** (Amount deposited) = 17,400 ÷ 1.45 = ₹ 12,000.

Value of **x** = (12,000 ÷ 80,000) × 100 = 15.

**∴ The correct answer is 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Total Salary** = ₹ 80,000

**Rate of Interest** (R) = 15% per annum

**Time Period** (T) = 3 years

**Accumulated Amount** (A) = ₹ 17,400

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P + SI = P × (1 + (R × T) ÷ 100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7ece97df2271a289df08189a4462f926d6bc1662436b9ddf040bca944faa21b8.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the **Principal** amount deposited be P.

⇒ P = x% of 80,000 = (x ÷ 100) × 80,000 = 800x

⇒ 17,400 = 800x × (1 + (15 × 3) ÷ 100)

⇒ 17,400 = 800x × (1 + 45 ÷ 100)

⇒ 17,400 = 800x × 1.45

⇒ 17,400 = 1,160x

⇒ x = 17,400 ÷ 1,160

⇒ x = 15

**∴ The correct answer is 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

It is the interest calculated only on the initial **Principal** for the entire duration. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Accumulated Amount

The total money returned after the time period, which includes the **Principal** and the **Interest**. A = P + SI.

Percentage Change

When a value increases by r% for n years in **Simple Interest**, the total increase is (r × n)% of the **Base Value**.

questions.question: Two persons A and B start from the same point. A walks at 5 km/h. After 't' hours B starts and catches A after 2 hours of his own walking. If B’s speed is 8 km/h, what is the value of 't'?

questions.question: Which type of crop cultivation systematically maintains soil fertility through the sequential cultivation of various crops?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Crop Rotation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Crop Rotation** is the systematic practice of growing a series of **dissimilar types of crops** in the same area in sequential seasons to optimize **soil nutrients**.
 
• This method maintains **soil fertility** by alternating **nutrient-exhaustive crops** (like cereals) with **nutrient-restorative crops** (like legumes).
 
• **Leguminous plants** included in the rotation contain **Rhizobium bacteria** in their root nodules, which facilitate **biological nitrogen fixation**, naturally enriching the soil.
 
• It effectively breaks the life cycles of **pests and diseases** that are host-specific, thereby reducing the need for **chemical pesticides** and improving **crop yield**.
 
• By varying **root depths** (alternating deep-rooted and shallow-rooted crops), it improves **soil structure** and prevents **soil erosion**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Relay cropping**:

 
 
• A method of **multiple cropping** where a second crop is seeded into an existing **standing crop** before the first one is harvested.
 
• It reduces **temporal wastage** and utilizes residual **soil moisture**, though it requires precise **timing and management**.
 
 
 
• **Monocropping**:
 
 
• The agricultural practice of growing a **single crop** year after year on the same land.
 
• Common in industrial farming for **wheat** or **corn**, it often leads to **soil depletion** and increased **pathogen buildup**.
 
 
 
• **Mixed Farming**:
 
 
• An integrated system where **crop production** is combined with **livestock raising** on the same farm.
 
• It provides **economic stability** and allows for the **recycling of nutrients** through animal manure.

questions.question: Addition reactions are characteristic of which type of hydrocarbons?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both alkynes and alkenes.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__Concept__** 

__
 
• **Addition reactions are typical of unsaturated hydrocarbons containing double or triple bonds. Therefore, both alkenes and alkynes readily undergo addition reactions.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Alkenes contain at least one carbon-carbon double bond (C=C), making them unsaturated hydrocarbons.**
 
• **Alkynes contain at least one carbon-carbon triple bond (C≡C), making them highly reactive toward addition reactions.**
 
• Addition reactions involve the addition of atoms or groups across multiple bonds, converting unsaturated compounds into saturated compounds.
 
• Common addition reactions include hydrogenation, halogenation, hydrohalogenation, and hydration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• **Alkanes**__

 __
 
• Saturated hydrocarbons having only single covalent bonds.
 
• General formula: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.
 
• Typically undergo substitution reactions rather than addition reactions.
 
 
 
• **Alkenes**__
 __
 
• Unsaturated hydrocarbons containing at least one C=C double bond.
 
• General formula: CₙH₂ₙ.
 
• Readily undergo addition reactions due to the presence of a π-bond.
 
 
 
• **Alkynes**__
 __
 
• Unsaturated hydrocarbons containing at least one C≡C triple bond.
 
• General formula: CₙH₂ₙ−₂.
 
• Can undergo multiple addition reactions because of two π-bonds.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogenation**__
 __
 
• Addition of hydrogen in the presence of catalysts such as nickel, palladium, or platinum.
 
• Converts unsaturated hydrocarbons into saturated hydrocarbons.
 
 
 
• **Halogenation**__
 
 
• Addition of halogens such as chlorine or bromine across double or triple bonds.
 
• Used as a test for unsaturation in organic compounds.

__
 
• The chemical interaction between metals and acids is primarily determined by the **Reactivity Series**, which ranks metals based on their ability to lose electrons.
 
• In this series, **Copper (Cu)** is located below **Hydrogen (H)**, making it a relatively unreactive or **noble metal** compared to alkali or alkaline earth metals.
 
• For a metal to react with a **dilute acid** like **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)** and liberate gas, it must be capable of displacing hydrogen ions from the solution.
 
• Since copper has a lower **oxidation potential** than hydrogen, it cannot reduce **H⁺ ions** into **Hydrogen gas (H₂)**.
 
• The **Standard Reduction Potential** for the Cu²⁺/Cu couple is **+0.34 V**, which is higher than the **0.00 V** of the **Standard Hydrogen Electrode**, confirming the reaction is thermodynamically non-spontaneous.

• These metals react with **dilute HCl** to form **metal salts** (like ZnCl₂) and release **Hydrogen gas**, which can be identified by a **pop sound** when tested with a burning splinter.
 
 
 
• **Reaction with Oxidizing Acids**:
 
 
• Although copper does not react with dilute HCl, it can react with **concentrated Nitric acid (HNO₃)** or **concentrated Sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄)**.

questions.question: What is formed when the male germ-cell from the pollen grain fuses with the female gamete in flowering plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zygote**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In flowering plants (**Angiosperms**), the process of **sexual reproduction** involves the fusion of male and female gametes, a process formally known as **syngamy** or **fertilization**.
 
• The **male germ-cell** is carried by the **pollen grain**, which is produced in the **anther** of the flower.
 
• The **female gamete** (egg cell) is located inside the **embryo sac**, which is itself contained within the **ovule** found in the **ovary**.
 
• When a pollen grain lands on the **stigma**, it germinates to form a **pollen tube** that grows through the **style** to reach the ovule.
 
• The fusion of the **haploid** male gamete (n) with the **haploid** female egg cell (n) results in the formation of a **diploid** cell (2n) called the **zygote**.
 
• The **zygote** is the primary cell that undergoes subsequent **mitotic divisions** to develop into an **embryo**, which eventually grows into a new plant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stigma**:

 
 
• It is the sticky or feathery receptive part of the **pistil** (gynoecium) that captures **pollen grains** during the process of **pollination**.
 
 
 
• **Pollen grain**:
 
 
• These are microscopic structures that represent the **male gametophyte** generation and contain the **generative cell** responsible for producing male gametes.

• The **position** of an object refers to its specific location at any given time within a defined space, which requires a **reference point** to be meaningful.

• The **Origin** is typically assigned the numerical value of **zero** for all coordinates (e.g., 0,0 in a 2D plane), allowing for the measurement of **distance** and **direction**.
 
• To describe the **motion** of an object, one must specify how its **position** changes relative to the **Origin** over a period of time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: If an element 'X' has two isotopes, X-35 and X-37, what is the average atomic mass of chlorine? (X-35 = 75% and X-37 = 25%)

__
 
• The **Average Atomic Mass** of an element is the weighted average of the atomic masses of its naturally occurring **isotopes** based on their relative abundance in nature.
 
• To determine the average atomic mass, the mass of each isotope is multiplied by its fractional abundance, and the products are summed: **Average Mass** = (Mass of Isotope 1 × % Abundance₁) + (Mass of Isotope 2 × % Abundance₂).
 
• For the element **Chlorine** (X), the standard average atomic mass of **35.5 u** is derived from its two primary isotopes, **Cl-35** and **Cl-37**, which exist in a relative ratio of approximately **3:1**.
 
• In this specific calculation, the distribution is taken as **75%** for **Cl-35** and **25%** for **Cl-37**.
 
• The mathematical derivation is: (35 × 75/100) + (37 × 25/100) = (35 × 0.75) + (37 × 0.25) = 26.25 + 9.25 = **35.5 u**.
 
• Fractional atomic masses, like 35.5, indicate that the element is a mixture of isotopes with different **neutron counts** rather than a single type of atom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• These are atoms of the same chemical element that possess the same number of **protons** (same **atomic number**) but a different number of **neutrons** (different **mass number**).

• Physical properties, such as **boiling points**, **density**, and **rate of diffusion**, vary because these properties depend on the mass of the atom.

__
 
• **Meristematic tissues** are specialized groups of plant cells that remain in a state of continuous **mitotic division** throughout the life of the plant.
 
• These cells are **undifferentiated** or **totipotent**, acting as the primary source of all new cells that eventually differentiate into various specialized tissues.
 
• The continuous division of these cells facilitates **primary growth**, which increases the length of the plant, and **secondary growth**, which increases the thickness or **girth** of the plant.
 
• Morphologically, meristematic cells are small, **isodiametric**, and possess a very high **nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio**, featuring a large **nucleus** and dense **cytoplasm** to support rapid replication.
 
• These cells lack **large central vacuoles** because their metabolic focus is on **protein synthesis** and **DNA replication** rather than storage or structural support.
 
• They are encased in thin **primary cell walls** made of **cellulose**, which provides the necessary flexibility for **cell elongation** and subsequent division.

questions.question: Which of the following is the method used for refining metals such as copper, zinc and silver?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electrolytic refining**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electrolytic refining** is a highly effective electrochemical process used to obtain high-purity metals from impure samples, achieving purity levels of up to **99.9 percent**.
 
• The setup consists of an **anode** made of the **impure metal** and a **cathode** made of a thin strip of **pure metal**.
 
• A solution of a soluble **metal salt** of the same metal being refined serves as the **electrolyte**; for instance, **acidified copper sulphate** is utilized during copper refining.
 
• Upon passing an **electric current**, metal ions from the anode dissolve into the electrolyte and are simultaneously deposited as pure metal onto the cathode.
 
• Impurities that do not dissolve in the electrolyte settle below the anode as **anode mud**, which often contains valuable metals like **Silver (Ag)**, **Gold (Au)**, and **Platinum (Pt)**.
 
• This technique is standard industrial practice for refining **Copper (Cu)**, **Zinc (Zn)**, **Nickel (Ni)**, **Silver (Ag)**, and **Gold (Au)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• Refers to the overarching chemical and physical processes used to obtain a metal from its **mineral ore**.
 
• Includes various stages such as **froth flotation**, **leaching**, and **roasting** depending on the reactivity of the metal.
 
 
 
• **Distillation**:
 
 
• A refining method specifically suited for **volatile metals** that possess a low **boiling point**.
 
• The impure metal is evaporated and the pure metal vapors are condensed, effectively separating them from non-volatile impurities; common for **Mercury (Hg)** and **Zinc (Zn)**.
 
 
 
• **Smelting**:
 
 
• A pyrometallurgical process where **metal oxides** are reduced to their elemental form by heating beyond the melting point.
 
• Typically involves a **reducing agent** like **Coke (Carbon)** or **Carbon Monoxide** to remove oxygen from ores, primarily used in the production of **Iron (Fe)** and **Lead (Pb)**.

• The **magnification (m)** produced by a spherical mirror is defined as the ratio of the image distance to the object distance with a negative sign, expressed by the formula **m = −v / u**, where **v** is the image distance and **u** is the object distance.

• **Convex Mirror Properties**:

• The **focal length (f)** of a convex mirror is always **positive**, as its principal focus lies behind the mirror.

• When plotting this relationship on a **Cartesian coordinate system**, time is traditionally placed on the **x-axis** (independent variable) and distance on the **y-axis** (dependent variable).
 
• At the starting instant of observation, where **time (t) = 0**, the **distance (s) covered** is also zero; this mathematical coordinate **(0,0)** is known as the **Origin**.
 
• The resulting graph for uniform motion is a **straight line** that originates from the **Origin**, provided the measurement starts from the initial reference point.
 
• The **slope** (gradient) of the straight line in a distance-time graph represents the **magnitude of speed**; a constant slope confirms that the speed is not changing over time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Origin (0,0)**:

 
 
• In **kinematics**, the origin represents the **reference point** or the initial state of an object before any motion or time has elapsed.
 
• It is the intersection of the **abscissa** and the **ordinate** where all coordinate values are null.
 
 
 
• **Non-Uniform Motion**:
 
 
• If an object covers unequal distances in equal intervals of time, the motion is **non-uniform** or **accelerated**.
 
• The **distance-time graph** for non-uniform motion is a **curve**, such as a parabola in cases of constant acceleration, rather than a straight line.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Slope**:
 
 
• A **steeper slope** indicates a **higher constant speed**, whereas a **gentler slope** indicates a **lower constant speed**.
 
• If the graph is a **horizontal line** parallel to the time axis, the slope is **zero**, meaning the object is at **rest** (stationary).

questions.question: Which of the following is observed in the case of the solubility of a gas in a liquid?

options.text: It decreases with an increase in temperature
It is not affected by temperature
It first increases and then decreases with an increase in temperature
It increases with an increase in temperature

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It decreases with an increase in temperature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The process of dissolving a **gas in a liquid** is generally an **exothermic process**, meaning that heat is evolved during the dissolution (Gas + Solvent ↔ Solution + Heat).
 
• According to **Le Chatelier's Principle**, if a system at equilibrium is subjected to an **increase in temperature**, the equilibrium will shift in the direction that absorbs heat (the endothermic direction).
 
• Since the dissolution is exothermic, an increase in temperature favors the reverse process, which is the **evolution of gas** from the liquid, thereby decreasing its **solubility**.
 
• From a molecular perspective, an **increase in temperature** provides more **kinetic energy** to the gas molecules dissolved in the liquid, allowing them to overcome the **intermolecular attractive forces** of the solvent and escape into the gas phase.
 
• This phenomenon is widely observed in nature; for example, as water temperature rises in summer, the amount of **dissolved oxygen** decreases, which can lead to **hypoxia** in aquatic ecosystems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Henry's Law**:

 
 
• This law states that at a **constant temperature**, the solubility of a gas in a liquid is directly proportional to the **partial pressure** of the gas above the liquid.
 
• The mathematical expression is **C = kP**, where C is the concentration of dissolved gas, k is **Henry's Law constant**, and P is the partial pressure.
 
 
 
• **Enthalpy of Solution (ΔHₛₒₗₙ)**:
 
 
• For gases, the **enthalpy change** during dissolution is typically negative (exothermic) because the **solute-solvent interactions** release more energy than is required to create space in the solvent.
 
 
 
• **Pressure Effects**:
 
 
• Unlike solids and liquids, the solubility of gases is significantly affected by **external pressure**. Increasing pressure increases solubility, a principle utilized in the production of **carbonated beverages**.

questions.question: How much work must be performed to increase the velocity of a car weighing 120 kg from 72 km/h to 108 km/h?

The correct answer is __**3.0 × 10⁴ J**__.

• To perform calculations in the **International System of Units (SI)**, velocities must be converted from km/h to **m/s** by multiplying with the factor **5/18**.
 
• Calculation for **u**: 72 × (5/18) = **20 m/s**.
 
• Calculation for **v**: 108 × (5/18) = **30 m/s**.
 
• The **Work-Energy Theorem** states that the **Work Done (W)** on an object is equal to the change in its **Kinetic Energy (K.E.)**.

• It is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it has magnitude but no direction.

• The conversion factor **5/18** comes from dividing 1000 meters (1 km) by 3600 seconds (1 hour).

questions.question: The centre of curvature (C) of a concave mirror is located ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**In front of the mirror**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **spherical mirror** is a mirror whose reflecting surface is part of a hollow sphere of glass. These mirrors are categorized into **concave** and **convex** types based on the direction of their curvature.
 
• A **concave mirror**, also known as a **converging mirror**, has a **reflecting surface** that is curved inwards, directed toward the center of the sphere.
 
• The **centre of curvature (C)** is defined as the center of the original hollow sphere of which the mirror forms a part. It is not located on the surface of the mirror but is a point in space.

• The imaginary straight line passing through the **pole** and the **centre of curvature** of a spherical mirror.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Law of Conservation of Mass**, established by **Antoine Lavoisier** in **1789**, dictates that mass is neither created nor destroyed during a **chemical reaction** in an isolated system.
 
• According to this scientific principle, the **total mass of the reactants** must be equivalent to the **total mass of the products** formed.
 
• In the given reaction, **Sodium (Na)** and **Chlorine (Cl)** act as the reactants that combine to produce **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**.
 
• To calculate the result, the mass of **sodium** (5.6 g) is added to the mass of **chlorine** (8.0 g), resulting in a sum of **13.6 g**.
 
• The balanced chemical equation for this process is **2Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl**, which consistently maintains the **stoichiometric** balance of mass.
 
• Mathematically, the expression is: **Mass of Reactants** (5.6 g + 8.0 g) = **Mass of Product** (13.6 g).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Isobars** are defined as atoms of different chemical elements that possess the same **mass number** (total number of nucleons) but different **atomic numbers**.
 
• The **mass number** (represented by **A**) is the sum of **protons** and **neutrons** in the atomic nucleus, whereas the **atomic number** (represented by **Z**) is the number of protons.
 
• Because isobars have different **atomic numbers**, they are different chemical elements and occupy different positions in the **Modern Periodic Table**.
 
• A primary example of isobars includes **Argon** (Z=18, A=40), **Potassium** (Z=19, A=40), and **Calcium** (Z=20, A=40). All three have 40 **nucleons**.
 
• Since the number of **electrons** differs in neutral atoms of isobars, they exhibit distinct **chemical properties** and **physical properties**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Isotopes**:

 
 
• Atoms of the same element that have the same **atomic number** (protons) but different **mass numbers**.
 
• They share identical **chemical properties** because they have the same electronic configuration.
 
 
 
• **Isotones**:
 
 
• Atoms of different elements that have the same number of **neutrons**.
 
• Calculated as: Neutron Number (N) = Mass Number (A) − Atomic Number (Z).
 
 
 
• **Chemical Properties**:
 
 
• These are determined by the **valence electrons** of an atom. Since isobars belong to different groups in the periodic table, their **reactivity** and bonding behavior vary significantly.

questions.question: The distance between the pole and the position of the object placed in front of a concave mirror is 120 cm. A real and inverted image is formed by this mirror on a screen at 40 cm from the pole of this mirror. What will be the focal length of this mirror?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**-30 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Cartesian sign convention**, the distance of the object (u) from the **pole** is always taken as negative because the object is placed to the left of the mirror. Therefore, **u = -120 cm**.
 
• A **real and inverted image** is formed in front of a **concave mirror**, meaning the image distance (v) is also negative. Given that the image is formed on a screen 40 cm from the pole, **v = -40 cm**.
 
• The relationship between the **focal length (f)**, the object distance (u), and the image distance (v) is defined by the **Mirror Formula**: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u.
 
• Substituting the given values into the formula: 1/f = 1/(-40) + 1/(-120).
 
• To solve the equation, find the **least common multiple (LCM)** of 40 and 120, which is 120. This leads to: 1/f = (-3 - 1) / 120.
 
• Simplifying the expression results in 1/f = -4 / 120. By taking the reciprocal, we find **f = -120 / 4 = -30 cm**.
 
• The negative sign confirms that the mirror is **concave**, as its **principal focus** lies in front of the reflecting surface.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirror**:

 
 
• It is often called a **converging mirror** because it reflects light rays inward to a single focal point.
 
• The **focal length** of a concave mirror is always **negative**, whereas for a **convex mirror**, it is always positive.
 
• When the object is placed at a distance greater than the focal length, the image produced is **real and inverted**.
 
 
 
• **Sign Convention Rules**:
 
 
• All distances are measured from the **pole (P)** of the mirror, which serves as the origin.
 
• Distances measured in the same direction as the **incident light** are positive, and those measured in the opposite direction are negative.
 
• The **real image** distance is negative because it is formed on the same side as the object, while **virtual images** have positive distances as they are formed behind the mirror.

questions.question:
Which of the following is/are NOT true about action reaction forces?

(i) Action reaction forces are unequal in magnitude and always act in the same direction.

(ii) Action reaction forces act on different bodies.

(iii) Action reaction forces act on the same body.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (i) and (iii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Statement (i) claims that action-reaction forces are unequal in magnitude and act in the same direction. According to **Newton's Third Law of Motion**, for every action, there is an **equal and opposite reaction**. This means the forces must have the same **numerical value** and directions separated by **180 degrees**. Hence, statement (i) is incorrect.
 
• Statement (ii) mentions that these forces act on different bodies. An action-reaction pair involves the **interaction between two separate objects** (e.g., Object A exerts a force on Object B, and Object B exerts a force on Object A). Because they act on different entities, they do not **cancel each other out** to produce equilibrium on a single body. Hence, statement (ii) is correct.
 
• Statement (iii) suggests that action-reaction forces act on the same body. By definition, a **force pair** represents the mutual interaction between **two different objects**. If both forces were applied to the same body, there would be no **external force** to initiate motion from a state of rest. Hence, statement (iii) is incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Fundamental properties of **Newton's Third Law** include:

 
 
• **Simultaneity**: The action and reaction forces occur **instantaneously**. There is no cause-and-effect time delay; one cannot exist without the other.
 
• **Nature of Forces**: Both forces in a pair must be of the **same physical category**. For instance, if the action is a **gravitational force**, the reaction must also be a gravitational force.
 
• **Mathematical Vector Form**: It is denoted as **F₁₂ = −F₂₁**, where the **negative sign** confirms that the vector directions are diametrically opposed.
 
• **Practical Application**: This principle explains the **recoil of a gun**, the movement of a **jet airplane**, and how a **swimmer** pushes water backward to move forward.

• **Convex Mirror Properties**:

The correct answer is __**1 × 10−³ M**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **pH value** of a solution is a mathematical representation of its **acidity** or **alkalinity**, defined as the negative logarithm (base 10) of the **molar concentration** of **hydrogen ions (H⁺)**.
 
• The fundamental formula used to determine pH is **pH = −log₁₀[H⁺]**, where **[H⁺]** is the concentration in **moles per liter (M)**.
 
• To calculate the **hydrogen ion concentration** when the pH is known, the equation is rearranged into its exponential form: **[H⁺] = 10−pH**.
 
• Given that the **pH is 3**, we substitute this value into the equation: **[H⁺] = 10−³**.
 
• This results in a concentration of **0.001 M**, which is expressed in scientific notation as **1 × 10−³ M**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The pH Scale**:

 
 
• Introduced by **S.P.L. Sørensen** in **1909**, the scale typically ranges from **0 to 14** at room temperature (**25°C**).
 
• A **pH of 7** indicates a **neutral solution**, such as **pure water**, where the concentrations of **H⁺** and **OH−** ions are equal.
 
• Solutions with a **pH less than 7** are classified as **acidic**, meaning they have a higher concentration of **hydrogen ions**.
 
• Solutions with a **pH greater than 7** are classified as **basic** or **alkaline**, containing a lower concentration of **hydrogen ions**.
 
 
 
• **Logarithmic Nature**:
 
 
• The **pH scale** is logarithmic, meaning each whole number change on the scale represents a **tenfold change** in ion concentration.
 
• A solution with **pH 3** has **10 times** the concentration of **H⁺ ions** compared to a solution with **pH 4**, and **100 times** the concentration compared to a solution with **pH 5**.
 
• In aqueous solutions, the product of **hydrogen ion** and **hydroxide ion** concentrations (**Kw**) is always **1 × 10−¹⁴** at **298 K**.

questions.question: A device often used in electric circuits to change the resistance without changing the voltage source is the ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rheostat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Rheostat** is a variable electrical resistor used to control the flow of **Electric Current** by manually increasing or decreasing resistance.
 
• It operates on the principle that the **Resistance** ($R$) of a conductor is directly proportional to its length ($L$); by moving a sliding contact (wiper), the effective length of the resistive wire in the circuit is adjusted.
 
• According to **Ohm’s Law** ($V = IR$), when the resistance is modified while keeping the **Voltage Source** ($V$) constant, the current ($I$) changes inversely, allowing for precise control of motor speeds or heater temperatures.
 
• These devices are typically constructed using a **Resistive Wire**, such as **Nichrome** or **Constantan**, wound around an insulating ceramic cylinder to handle the heat generated by the resistance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ammeter**:

 
 
• An instrument designed to measure the **Electric Current** in a circuit in **Amperes**.
 
• It is always connected in **Series** with the circuit component and possesses exceptionally **Low Resistance** to avoid altering the circuit current.
 
 
 
• **Voltmeter**:
 
 
• Used to measure the **Potential Difference** between two points in an electrical circuit in **Volts**.
 
• It is connected in **Parallel** and has **High Resistance** to ensure it draws negligible current from the main circuit.
 
 
 
• **Fuse**:
 
 
• A safety device consisting of a thin wire with a **Low Melting Point** that melts and breaks the circuit during an **Overload** or **Short Circuit**.
 
• It acts as a sacrificial component to protect expensive electrical appliances from damage caused by **Excessive Current**.

questions.question: The rough endoplasmic reticulum is associated with:
questions.solution:
**1) Protein synthesis**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER) is primarily responsible for the synthesis and folding of proteins.**
 
• It is called "rough" because its outer surface is studded with **ribosomes**, which are the actual sites where amino acids are assembled into polypeptide chains.
 
• The RER is particularly abundant in cells that are actively involved in **protein secretion**, such as the cells of the pancreas that produce digestive enzymes or plasma cells that produce antibodies.
 
• Once proteins are synthesized on the ribosomes, they enter the lumen of the RER, where they undergo **post-translational modifications**, such as folding and the addition of carbohydrates (glycosylation).
 
• The RER also acts as a quality control center, ensuring that misfolded proteins are identified and either refolded or targeted for degradation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lipid synthesis:** This function is associated with the **Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER)**. Unlike the RER, the SER lacks ribosomes. It is responsible for the synthesis of essential lipids such as phospholipids and cholesterol, as well as the production of steroid hormones. Additionally, the SER plays a crucial role in the detoxification of drugs and poisons, especially in liver cells.
 
• **DNA replication:** This process takes place within the **Nucleus** of eukaryotic cells. DNA replication is the biological process of producing two identical replicas of DNA from one original DNA molecule. It occurs during the S-phase of the cell cycle to ensure that each daughter cell receives a complete set of genetic information.
 
• **Enzyme breakdown:** The degradation or breakdown of organic molecules and worn-out cell parts is the primary function of **Lysosomes**. These are membrane-bound organelles containing digestive enzymes (hydrolases). They are often referred to as the "suicidal bags" of the cell because they can digest the cell itself if it becomes damaged or dies.
 
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER):** This is a continuous membrane system that forms a series of flattened sacs (cisternae) within the cytoplasm. It serves as a major site for metabolic processes and provides a transport network for moving materials within the cell.
 
• **Ribosomes:** These are small, dense granules found either floating freely in the cytoplasm or attached to the RER. They are composed of RNA and proteins and serve as the molecular machines that translate genetic code into proteins.

Prokaryotic cell : Small and simple :: Eukaryotic cell : _______
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The analogy compares the structural characteristics of two primary cell types: **Prokaryotic** and **Eukaryotic**.
 
• **Prokaryotic cells**, such as **Bacteria** and **Archaea**, are termed **small and simple** because they lack a membrane-bound **nucleus** and other specialized organelles. Their size typically ranges from **0.1 to 5.0 micrometers**.
 
• **Eukaryotic cells**, found in **Plants**, **Animals**, and **Fungi**, are significantly **larger**, generally measuring between **10 to 100 micrometers** in diameter.
 
• These cells are considered **complex** due to **internal compartmentalization**, where specific metabolic functions are isolated within membrane-bound organelles like the **mitochondria**, **endoplasmic reticulum**, and **Golgi apparatus**.
 
• Unlike the simple structure of prokaryotes, eukaryotes possess a well-defined **nucleus** that serves as the control center, protecting the cell's **genetic material**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Genetic Material Organization**:

 
 
• In **Prokaryotes**, DNA is typically a single, **circular chromosome** located in an irregular region called the **nucleoid**.
 
• In **Eukaryotes**, DNA is organized into multiple **linear chromosomes** associated with **histone proteins**.
 
 
 
• **Cell Division Processes**:
 
 
• Prokaryotes reproduce primarily through **binary fission**, a relatively rapid and straightforward asexual process.
 
• Eukaryotes undergo **mitosis** for growth and **meiosis** for sexual reproduction, involving complex stages of chromosome alignment and separation.
 
 
 
• **Ribosome Differences**:
 
 
• Prokaryotes contain smaller **70S ribosomes**.
 
• Eukaryotes contain larger **80S ribosomes** in the cytoplasm, though they also have 70S ribosomes within their **mitochondria** and **chloroplasts**.

questions.question: By which act did the British government introduce provincial autonomy in India instead of diarchy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Government of India Act 1935**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of India Act 1935** was a landmark legislation that introduced **Provincial Autonomy**, granting provinces a separate legal identity and autonomy in their executive and legislative spheres.
 
• This Act abolished the system of **Diarchy** (dual government) in the provinces, which had been previously established under the **Government of India Act 1919**.
 
• The abolition of **Diarchy** meant that the distinction between **Transferred** and **Reserved** subjects at the provincial level was removed, making the provincial executive responsible to the **Provincial Legislature**.
 
• It provided for the appointment of a **Governor** who was advised by ministers, and these ministers were collectively responsible to the elected provincial assembly.
 
• While it ended **Diarchy** in provinces, the Act proposed the introduction of **Diarchy at the Center**, though the federal portion of the Act was never fully operationalized.
 
• The Act also laid the foundation for an **All-India Federation** consisting of British Indian provinces and **Princely States**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Government of India Act 1919**:

 
 
• Also known as the **Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms**, it introduced **Diarchy** in provinces.
 
• It established a **Bicameral Legislature** at the central level for the first time.
 
 
 
• **Indian Councils Act 1909**:
 
 
• Known as the **Morley-Minto Reforms**, it is infamous for introducing **Separate Electorates** for Muslims.
 
• It increased the size of legislative councils and allowed members to discuss the **Budget** and ask supplementary questions.
 
 
 
• **Indian Councils Act 1892**:
 
 
• This act expanded the number of non-official members in the councils and introduced a limited form of **indirect elections**.
 
• It empowered the legislative councils to discuss the **Annual Financial Statement** and address questions to the executive.

questions.question: As part of trade liberalization, in which year did India completely remove Quantitative Restrictions (QRs) on imports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2001**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Quantitative Restrictions (QRs)** are non-tariff barriers, such as **quotas** and **import licensing**, used by a government to limit the physical quantity of goods that can be imported over a specific period.
 
• India maintained these restrictions for decades to protect domestic industries and manage **Balance of Payments (BoP)** crises, citing the provisions under the **General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)**.
 
• Following the **Economic Reforms of 1991**, India began a systematic process of **Trade Liberalization** to integrate its economy with the global market.
 
• A significant turning point occurred when the **World Trade Organization (WTO)** ruled against India in a dispute triggered by the **United States**, stating that India’s improved BoP position no longer justified the maintenance of QRs.
 
• Consequently, India committed to a phased removal of these barriers. The final batch of **715 items**, which included **agricultural products** and **consumer goods**, saw the total elimination of QRs on **April 1, 2001**.
 
• This move marked the transition from a **command-based licensing regime** to a **market-linked tariff system**, significantly impacting the **Exim Policy (Export-Import Policy)** of the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **New Economic Policy (1991)**:

 
 
• Commonly referred to as the **LPG Model** (Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization), it was spearheaded by then Finance Minister **Dr. Manmohan Singh**.
 
• It aimed to reduce the **License-Permit Raj**, encourage **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**, and dismantle **trade barriers** to boost industrial efficiency.
 
 
 
• **World Trade Organization (WTO)**:
 
 
• Established on **January 1, 1995**, following the **Uruguay Round** of negotiations, it serves as the global body regulating international trade.
 
• India is a **founding member** and is obligated to adhere to its principles of **most-favored-nation (MFN)** treatment and the reduction of protectionist measures.
 
 
 
• **Tariffication**:
 
 
• After removing QRs, India shifted to **Tariffs** (customs duties) as the primary tool for regulating imports, which is considered a more transparent and less distortionary method of **trade protection**.
